evidence_read: Growers record trees in dedicated apps, spreadsheets, photo systems, notes, notebooks and hybrid workflows.
Daily, multi-month, since-launch and 2+ year paid-use cases exist.
Uninstall, structured-record abandonment and developer-acknowledged bug/stability churn exist.
App→app, app→desktop, app→general tools and structured system→photo metadata are observed.
Excel, Photos, OneNote, Evernote, Lightroom, phone notes/alarms and paper can satisfy enough of the job for some users.
limitation: Incremental advantage required to beat them is unmeasured.

evidence_read: Per-tree repetition, too many fields, photo handling and high collection size can make capture tedious.
Search, filters, batching, organization and retrieval become salient as collections grow.
Users repeatedly value photos and seeing development over time.
limitation: Does not imply dedicated software is required.

evidence_read: Users value reminders for planned work and memory.
limitation: Generic/date-driven reminders can create noise or false precision.

evidence_read: Data-loss incidents, export questions and software-longevity concern affect trust.
Subscription conversion, paid multi-year use and simultaneous paid-product comparison are observed.
limitation: WTP distribution and economics remain unvalidated.

evidence_read: Some users explicitly reject SaaS/subscriptions or require clear value over free tools.
Beginners lean toward guidance/reassurance; experienced growers lean toward history, flexibility, custom rules and continuity.

theme: Cumulative value vs repeated maintenance cost
evidence_read: History/progression value can accumulate while capture cost recurs on every interaction.
Incorrect/generic advice carries higher trust cost than neutral recordkeeping.
Some users value seeing other trees/progression.
Competitors ship transfer/history; reviews rarely identify evidence/attestation as adoption or retention value.
Progression/comparable cases have public learning value.
W1 constrains the opportunity but does not select a product.
